evidence: Cic. Att. 1.17.6: sermōnis commūnicātiō quae mihi suāvissima tēcum solet esse
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “a making common, imparting, communicating”, found “several times in Cic., elsewh. rare”; with sermōnis, the exchange of talk, with cōnsiliī, of plans (Cic. Fam. 5.19.2).

terms.gloss: dealings, an exchange (of words or letters)
evidence: Sen. Ep. 38.1: hoc inter nōs epistulārum commercium
Tac. Agr. 2.3 (Lewis & Short): loquendī audiendīque commercium
terms.comment: Literally trade. Lewis & Short: “intercourse, communication, correspondence”; sermōnis commercium (Liv. 5.15.5).

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation; aliquid cum aliquō

phrases.latin: quīn mihi nunc tē absente nōn sōlum cōnsilium quō tū excellis, sed etiam sermōnis commūnicātiō quae mihi suāvissima tēcum solet esse, maximē deest
phrases.english: now that you are away, what I miss most is not only your advice, in which you excel, but also the talks we share, which are always the sweetest thing to me

phrases.latin: Meritō exigis, ut hoc inter nōs epistulārum commercium frequentēmus.
phrases.english: You are right to insist that we keep up this exchange of letters between us.

sources: Lewis & Short: communicatio · Lewis & Short: commercium · Lewis & Short: communico
Cic. Att. 1.17.6 and Off. 1.50, Sen. Ep. 38.1 checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
